title: Count Good Integers in a Range
summary: Given integers l, r, and k, count how many numbers in the range [l, r] have an absolute difference of at most k between every pair of adjacent digits.
statement: Given integers l, r, and k, count how many numbers in the range [l, r] have an absolute difference of at most k between every pair of adjacent digits.
constraints: An integer is good when every adjacent decimal digit differs by at most k.
Count both endpoints when they satisfy the rule.
hints: Count valid values up to one bound, then subtract the count below the left endpoint.
A digit-DP state needs position, previous significant digit, whether the number started, and tightness.
Leading zeros do not participate in adjacency checks; once started, accept a digit only within k of the previous digit.
Memoization collapses all equal suffix states, giving work proportional to digit count rather than interval width.
